question: Which of the five has been most explicit about serving mass-affluent clients, and what exactly have they said?

cells.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones states it primarily serves individual investors in the U.S. and Canada, and is committed to helping improve the financial fulfillment for tens of millions of long-term investors across North America by providing comprehensive, personalized planning and professional advice.
items.quote: the Partnership primarily serves individual investors in the U.S. and Canada... the Firm is committed to helping improve the financial fulfillment for tens of millions of long-term investors across North America by providing comprehensive, personalized planning and professional advice

items.text: Edward Jones states its strategic ambition is to improve the financial wellness for tens of millions of long-term investors across North America.
items.quote: the Partnership's strategic ambition to improve the financial wellness for tens of millions of long-term investors across North America

cells.reason: The passages describe Edward Jones's stated clientele as individual/long-term investors across North America broadly rather than specifically using the term 'mass-affluent.'

cells.label: fact

items.text: Edward Jones's new initiatives target specific client groups: High Net Worth, Workplace (local business owners and their employees), and a new digital platform for Next Generation investors; it does not name a mass-affluent segment.
items.quote: These initiatives also include targeting new clients: High Net Worth, focused on attracting and serving high net worth clients...; Workplace, which connects local business owners and their employees...; and a new digital platform, focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors.

cells.reason: This is the most explicit description of Edward Jones's client-targeting strategy, and it identifies high net worth, business owners/employees, and next generation investors rather than mass-affluent.
